## cloud/account

Making a sync account and signing a device in to one: the
keys made from the passphrase here, the account key made here or
unwrapped here, and the server told only what signs in.

The account key is wrapped twice: under the passphrase, and under a
recovery code, made with the account and shown once. Either signs in. A
change to either takes the passphrase typed again (or the code, to set a
new passphrase), since a device keeps only keys made from the account key,
not the key itself. Signing in with the code sets a new passphrase and
makes a new code in its place.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Keys".

## ACCOUNT

Type: [string][684]

## ACCOUNT

Type: [string][684]

## ACCOUNT

Type: [string][684]

## ACCOUNT

Type: [string][684]

## ACCOUNT

What the account key is sealed as, under the wrapping key.

Type: [string][684]

## recoveryFor

A new recovery code for an account key: the code to show, and what the
server keeps of it.

### Parameters

- `secret` **Bytes**&#x20;

## readRecoveryCode

Type: [string][684]

## readRecoveryCode

A recovery code as typed back, read the way Crockford's base 32 is: any
case, I and L as 1, O as 0, spaces and dashes ignored.

### Parameters

- `typed` **[string][684]**&#x20;

Returns **([string][684] | null)** Its 25 letters, or null for what isn't one

## SHORTEST_PASSPHRASE

The fewest characters a new passphrase may have. Whoever holds the
server's database can try passphrases against it as fast as the key
derivation lets them; one signing in is not held to it.

Type: [number][685]

## longEnough

Refuse a new passphrase too short to stand up to that.

### Parameters

- `passphrase` **[string][684]**&#x20;

## passphraseFor

What the server keeps of a passphrase for an account key.

### Parameters

- `passphrase` **[string][684]**&#x20;
- `secret` **Bytes**&#x20;
- `kdf` **[Kdf][138]**&#x20;

## signUp

Make an account, and sign this device in to it.

- `passphrase` **[string][684]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][687]<{secret: Bytes, auth: Bytes}>**&#x20;

## remakeRecovery

Make a new recovery code, in place of the one there was.

### Parameters

- `api` **Api** As this device signed in
- `passphrase` **[string][684]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][687]<[string][684]>** The code, to show once

## changePassphrase

Change the passphrase. Devices signed in stay so.

### Parameters

- `api` **Api** As this device signed in
- `$1` **[Object][686]**&#x20;
  - `$1.current` &#x20;
  - `$1.next` &#x20;
  - `$1.kdf` (optional, default `KDF`)

## recover

Sign this device in with a recovery code, and set a new passphrase. The
code is used up: a new one is made in its place.

### Parameters

- `api` **Api**&#x20;
- `$1` **[Object][686]**&#x20;
  - `$1.name` &#x20;
  - `$1.code` &#x20;
  - `$1.passphrase` &#x20;
  - `$1.device` &#x20;
  - `$1.kdf` (optional, default `KDF`)

- `as` &#x20;

<!---->

- Throws **[Error][688]** For what isn't a recovery code

Returns **[Promise][687]<{token: [string][684], keys: [AccountKeys][141], recoveryCode: [string][684]}>**&#x20;

## recover

Sign in with a recovery code's sign-in key.

### Parameters

- `name` **[string][684]**&#x20;
- `auth` **Bytes**&#x20;
- `device` **[string][684]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][687]<{token: [string][684], key: Bytes}>** The account key wrapped under the code

## cloud/api

The sync server, as the device asks it: JSON over HTTP with
a bearer token, bytes as base64, a file's parts as they are, and a stream
of the collections that changed.

The design is `.llm/sync_design.md`, "The protocol".

## HOSTED_SERVER

Type: [string][684]

## HOSTED_SERVER

Our sync service, the only server a build without dev features (`config/dev.js`) signs in to.

Type: [string][684]

## CloudError

**Extends Error**

A request the server refused, or one that never reached it.

## cloud/crypto

The keys sync is encrypted with, and what is done with them,
all on the device: the server gets ciphertext, hashed names, and a key
that signs in but opens nothing.

- The **passphrase**, through PBKDF2 and a salt the account keeps, gives a
  master secret, which HKDF splits into the **sign-in key**, sent to the
  server, and the **wrapping key**, which never leaves the device.
- The **account key** is random. The server keeps it wrapped, and a device
  keeps what it makes (a key to wrap collection keys with, and a key to
  name collections with) as CryptoKeys that can't be exported.
- A **recovery code** is random as well: 25 characters of Crockford's
  base 32, 125 bits, too many to guess however fast each guess is, so HKDF
  alone makes its own sign-in key and wrapping key, and the server keeps
  the account key wrapped under it a second time.
- Each **collection's key** is random too, and kept wrapped under the
  account's. HKDF makes from it the key its records are encrypted with
  and the key their names are hashed with.
- For sharing, an account has a **key pair** (ECDH on P-256): the server
  keeps the public half, and the private half sealed under the account
  key. A collection shared is wrapped for a friend's public key, and the
  friend found by a **friend code**, the public key's fingerprint, which
  the server can't forge a key for. In a shared collection a chat is its
  writer's **own**, sealed under a key their account makes from the
  collection's id, which no other account has.

Everything sealed is AES-GCM with a random nonce before the ciphertext,
and with what it is (a collection and a record's name) as additional
data, so that a body moved to another record does not open there.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Keys".

## cloud/diagnostics

What the sync engine counts of how syncing goes, for the
sync server: rounds and their failures, records and bytes each way,
conflicts and clashes, trees repaired, rows the start-up check found
unsent, the outbox's length, files fetched. Counts and fixed tags only:
never text, titles, names, ids or error messages, so the report tells the
server nothing it doesn't see already.

`useCloudSync` sends a report every quarter of an hour and when the page
is hidden, unless the writer turned them off or the server wants none.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Hosted", "Seeing what happens".

## cloud/engine

Sync's rounds: what this device wrote, sent; what the others
wrote, brought in; and the two merged where both changed one row.

Every write to a project reaches `noteWrite`, from the storage facade,
and is put in the **outbox** by its row, the row as written. Beside it
the device keeps a **record** of each row as the server last had it: its
revision, a fingerprint, and for the rows merged three ways the row
itself, the base of the next merge. A **round** then:

1.  Lists the collections, and pulls each project this window syncs from
    where it last read up to. A row with nothing waiting here is written
    here as it came. One with something waiting is merged, and the merge
    is written here and waits to go back.
2.  Pushes the outbox, each row against the revision it was based on. A
    row the server took leaves the outbox; one that moved on meanwhile
    comes back, is merged as in a pull, and goes in the next round.
3.  Fetches the bytes this device lacks that it wants at once: pictures,
    which their documents show. A file's bytes are fetched when they are
    wanted (`fetchFile`): when the file is opened, converted or backed up.

Beside the projects, the account has a collection of its own: the
writer's setup and card library (`cloud/setup.js`). Its rows are kept as a
project's are, under `SETUP` where a project's are under its story's id,
and merged the same way. It carries no meta, so an app from before it was
synced passes over it; this one knows it by its id, made from the
account's key. A device's first sync of it puts the whole setup in the
outbox, as a first sync does every project; where the account has a row
already, the account's stands, and a row this device made as every install
makes it is never sent, so that a new device's defaults stand over nobody's.

A merge can leave a project's tree broken in ways neither device made it:
a document whose folder is gone, a loop, two siblings of one name
(`cloud/tree.js`). The engine looks at the tree of each project a pull
brought documents to, and puts right what is still wrong a while later:
what another device sends in two pushes can be seen between them, a child
before its folder.

A write is put in the outbox just after it is made, and a page closed
between the two loses it to sync. Once a launch, and when the writer asks
for a sync, the engine compares every row here with the server's as it
last had it, and puts in the outbox those that differ (`check`). Only
changes: a row missing here could as well be one that couldn't be read,
and a removal sent for it would remove it everywhere.

What the engine writes here comes back to it through the facade like any
other write; it expects those, and leaves them out of the outbox.

A server put back from a backup has gone back in time: it may lack what
it answered for since. It says so with a new generation, and the engine
then syncs as on a first sync, every row it has sent again, so that
nothing it wrote is lost.

A project the writer keeps on this device only (`syncOff` on its story)
is left out of every round: its writes never wait to go, and what the
server has of it, nothing. Kept off, it is taken off the server once, by
a round, as a project kept rather than deleted. The other devices move
their copies to their trash and keep them out of sync as well
(`keptElsewhere`), until the project is on the server again; synced
again, it goes up whole, as on a first sync, and they take it back.

A record written by a newer app, in a newer schema or format
(`cloud/format.js`), holds its project's pull where it is until this app
is updated: what came before it is written here, and it and what came
after wait on the server. The device still sends what it writes, but a row
a newer app wrote since waits in the outbox, unmerged, since a merge here
would lose what that app knows. The status says sync waits for an update.

A project is shared with friends by their friend codes (`share`): the
project's key wrapped for each one's public key, which their first device
wraps again under their account key as it first sees the project, and
which it then brings in as a project made elsewhere. In a shared project a
chat and its messages are their writer's own: sealed under a key only
that account makes, and served by the server to it alone. Sharing sends
the owner's chats again so before anyone else has the key, and the server
takes a push to a shared project only from a device that knows it is
shared. Who is in each shared project is asked again as the number
changes, and told to the app (`onSharing`). A friend who left, or was
removed, has the project moved to the trash, out of sync, as one another
device kept to itself; one the owner deleted goes as for its owner, but
with edits waiting it stays here in the trash, out of sync, rather than
go up again.

A project its owner shares with only some of its documents hides the
others from everyone it is shared with: they go as the owner's own, their
files and versions with them, and what the others had of them goes with a
removal for them (`regroup`). The folders on the way to what is shared go
as everyone's (`cloud/tree.js`), so the tree holds together for them.

Past the account's quota, the server refuses what would take more room,
record by record, and a file's parts; those wait in the outbox, the rest
syncs, and the status says the storage is full.

The engine counts what it does for the server's diagnostics
(`cloud/diagnostics.js`): counts and tags, never content.

The engine knows nothing of the stores: `Local` is how it reaches the
app, and `State` where it keeps the outbox, the records and how far it has
read (IndexedDB, in the app).

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "On the device".

## cloud/format

What a synced row may hold, as a number every record carries
beside its schema. The schema follows the tables; the format follows what
is in them: the markup a document's text may hold, the fields a row may
have and what they mean. An app that meets a record of a newer format, or
a newer schema, holds that project's pull until it is updated, since its
editor would drop markup it doesn't know, and its stores fields, as it
saved over them.

A record carries the oldest format that holds it, so that an older app is
held only by a record it would harm, and a project with none of them goes
on syncing with it.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Schema versions".

## FORMAT

The newest format this app reads, and so the newest a record it writes may
carry. Raise it by one when a synced row may come to hold what an older app
would lose or change on its way through: the editor learning a node, a
mark or an attribute, new markup in a document's text, or a field coming
to mean something else; and say in `formatOf` which records carry it. A
new table or index raises the schema instead. Records from before formats
carry none, which reads as 0.

Type: [number][685]

## FIRST

What every record has carried at the least since formats began, 21 Oct 2026.

Type: [number][685]

## TEXT_FORMAT

The format a document is written in for its text: what the editor holds
(`editor/schema.js`, which a test pins to it). Raised with `FORMAT` when
the editor learns a node, a mark or an attribute, or a text may hold new
markup.

Type: [number][685]

## HELD_FORMAT

The format a document held by a text or an imported file is written in,
rather than by a folder (`.llm/nested_documents_design.md`). An older
desktop app lays one out at the top of its project on disk, reads it back
from there, and sends that on as a move.

Type: [number][685]

## formatOf

The format a record is written in: the oldest that holds it.

- `row` **any** The row it sends; null for one it removes
- `parentType` **[string][684]?** For a document, its parent's type, when its
  parent is a document here

Returns **[number][685]**&#x20;

## cloud

Sync: the writer's projects, setup and card library kept in
step across their devices through a server of ours that can't read them.

Each device keeps its own whole copy and works offline; the server keeps
every project as a collection of records it can't read, the setup as one
more, and answers what changed since a revision. A project can be shared
with friends by their friend codes, each one's chats in it their own. The
devices do everything that needs the content: encrypting it, merging what
two of them changed, and writing what came in where the app reads it. The
server is a program of its own, kept apart from the app.

- **crypto** - The keys, made from the passphrase and at random, and what
  is sealed and hashed with them
- **account** - Making an account and signing a device in to one, and
  keeping it safe: the recovery code, a new passphrase
- **deviceName** - What a device calls itself in the account's list
- **api** - The server, as the device asks it
- **merge** - One row as two devices changed it, merged against the base
- **format** - What a synced row may hold, as a number beside its schema:
  a record of a newer one holds the pull until the app is updated
- **engine** - The rounds: the outbox sent, what others wrote brought in,
  the two merged, files' bytes in parts
- **local** - The app as the engine reaches it: the stores for what is
  loaded, storage for the rest
- **setup** - The writer's setup as sync sends it: which tables and
  settings, and what of them stays on the device
- **people** - Who is who, for sharing: this account, who is in each
  project shared, and whose a comment's post is

`composables/useCloudSync` signs in and out and runs the rounds; Settings
› Sync and sharing is where the writer does it, always with
`sync.inksprite.io` but in a build with dev features (`config/dev.js`).

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`.

## cloud/invite

An invitation to a sync server, opened as a link:
`https://app.inksprite.io/?server=sync.inksprite.io&invite=7K3M-Q9TX-2HDP`.

Opening it takes the server and the code off the address, and has the
settings open on Sync, ready to create an account with them. The server
counts only in a build with dev features (`config/dev.js`); any other signs
up with ours, so a link can't send a writer's account elsewhere. The admin
script prints the link (`server/src/admin.js invite`).

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Hosted", "Accounts".

## cloud/local

The app as sync's engine reaches it: projects read whole for
a first sync, and what other devices wrote written here.

What comes in goes where the app reads it. A project whose tree this
window has loaded takes it through the stores, so that what is in memory
and what is stored stay one; a document open in the editor takes its new
text as an outside edit, merged with whatever was typed since the round
began. Anything not loaded is written straight to storage. Either way it
comes back through the storage facade to the engine, which expects it.

The text that lost a clash is kept as a version of its document, named
so that it never ages out, without a word: the merge has picked a winner,
and the version is there to go back to. Without versions, it is kept as a
conflict copy beside the document.

The setup, the account's own collection (`cloud/setup.js`), is written to
the app tables and the settings, and the stores that read those tables
read them again, in this window as in the others.

In the desktop app each window syncs the projects it holds, and the
window syncing for the app syncs the rest and the setup
(`platform/windows.js`).

## cloud/merge

One row as two devices changed it, merged: against the base,
the row as both last had it from the server, where there is one.

A document's text is merged three ways, line by line, and within lines
both sides changed, word by word. Lines both put in at one place are kept
both, this device's first. Where the two changed the same words, they
**clash**, and this device's stand: it is the one syncing later. The
other's whole text is handed back, to be kept as a version, so nothing
either wrote is lost. A clash of a paragraph or two leaves the rest merged;
a larger one, as after a long time offline, leaves this device's text
whole, since half of one rewrite around the other's edits reads worse
than either. The text is merged as text, marks and all: comment marks are
in it, and a comment made on one device is kept by a merge with the other.

The other fields of a document, and a story's and a chat's, are merged one
by one, a document's threads and pictures by their ids: a field changed
on one side takes that side's, and one changed on both takes the newer
row's. Messages and files have no base kept, and the newer wins.

Without a base, as on a device's first sync of a project another device
has too, the newer row wins, and a text document whose text differs hands
back the other's as a large clash.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Merging".

## cloud/names

What a sync account may be called: 3 to 30 of the letters a
to z, digits and hyphens, a hyphen only between two others, and none of
the names the server keeps back. Checked here as an account is made, so
the writer hears at once; the server holds to the same
(`server/src/names.js`), and keeps back the names. An account made before
signs in as it is.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Hosted", "Accounts".

## cloud/onDemand

Files' bytes that sync leaves on the server until they are
wanted, as the app asks for them.

A device syncing a project takes its files' records at once, and their
text is already their documents' content, which the tree, search and the
model read. The bytes, a rulebook's two hundred megabytes, stay on the
server until something wants the file itself: the viewer, a conversion, a
download, a backup. Then they are fetched and kept.

Sync provides the fetching while the device is signed in
(`composables/useCloudSync`); with no account, there is nothing elsewhere.
Kept apart from sync so that the files store can ask without importing
it, which imports the files store.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Files".

## cloud/people

Who is who, for sharing: the account this device is signed in
to, and who is in each project shared, as sync last heard (`useCloudSync`
keeps them here). Kept apart from sync itself so that what shows a
comment's author needn't load it.

A comment's post written on a device signed in to sync says which account
wrote it (`by`). In a project shared, a post is the writer's own when that
is this account, and one with none, from before, is its owner's; anyone
else's is under their name.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Sharing".

## People

The people of one project shared, for naming a post's author.

- `owner` **([number][685] | null)** The project's owner
- `names` **Record<[number][685], ([string][684] | null)>** Each one's name, by account

## cloud/setup

The writer's setup as sync sends it: the account's own
collection, beside each project's.

It holds the rows of the app tables a setup is made of (connections with
their keys, presets, prompts, chat profiles, MCP servers, skills and their
wordings, web search) and the card library, and the settings kept outside
the database that a settings file carries, a group to a row. What is the
device's own stays out: Debug, Compact text, whether the spell checker is
on, where the panels are, the projects' views, and the sign-ins that
refresh (MCP servers' and Google's, never on a row).

The engine keeps the collection's rows under `SETUP` where a project's
would be under its story's id. A story's id is `story_…`, so the two never
meet.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "The account's own collection".

## SETUP

Type: [string][684]

## SETUP

Type: [string][684]

## SETUP

What the account's collection is kept under, in place of a story's id.

Type: [string][684]

## SETUP_TABLES

The app tables the setup is made of, the card library's two among them.

## SETTINGS

The settings kept outside the database, as rows of the collection: one a group.

Type: [string][684]

## DEVICE_SPELLING

Of the spelling settings, the device's own: a phone keeps its keyboard's checker.

## idOf

What a row of the setup is known by in its table: a skill's wording by its
skill's name, the rest by their ids.

### Parameters

- `table` **[string][684]**&#x20;
- `row` **any**&#x20;

Returns **([string][684] | [undefined][694])**&#x20;

A row of the setup as it is sent, without what is this device's alone: a
key the writer chose not to keep, why a server couldn't be listed here,
and a card's picture, whose bytes go as a file's do.

### Parameters

- `table` **[string][684]**&#x20;
- `row` **any**&#x20;

Returns **any**&#x20;

How long after it was made a row can say it was changed, and have been changed by nobody.

Type: [number][685]

## asMade

Whether a row is one every install makes on its first start, as it made
it: a built-in connection with nothing of the writer's in it, or the
default preset never changed since. Such a row is never sent first, so
that a new device signed in before the one with the setup doesn't make its
empty defaults the account's.

### Parameters

- `table` **[string][684]**&#x20;
- `row` **any**&#x20;

Returns **[boolean][689]**&#x20;

## cloud/tree

A project's tree as two devices' changes, merged, can leave
it, and what puts it right.

Each device keeps its tree whole, but a merge takes each document's fields
on their own, and the two together can make what neither did:

- **A document whose folder is gone**: moved into a folder on one device
  while that folder was deleted for good on the other.
- **A loop**: one device moved a folder into a second while the other moved
  the second into the first.
- **Two siblings of one name**: a "Chapter 3" made in one folder on each
  device, which the app never lets happen on one.

The first two go to the project's root, after what is there; of two
siblings of one name, the one made first keeps it, and the other takes the
next free one, "Chapter 3 (2)". The fixes depend on the rows alone, so two
devices that see the same tree make the same ones, and their merge agrees.

A project shared with only some of its documents hides the others from
those it is shared with (`hiddenDocuments`), never a folder on the way to
something shared: a friend's device would take the document for one whose
folder is gone. A document that holds others is never on the way, since
its own text and file would go with it: what is under one goes only with
it.

Design: `.llm/sync_design.md`, "Merging".

### Parameters

- `documents` &#x20;
- `storyId` &#x20;
- `now` &#x20;
